Data source overview (2-3 sentences):
The text summarizes the Machine Intelligence Research Institute’s (MIRI) public position that catastrophic AI misalignment is a severe, unsolved technical risk. MIRI argues that only mathematically-formal, security-mindset–driven alignment research—pursued along many independent directions—offers meaningful hope, whereas policy solutions alone are viewed as ineffective.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[82] – The source is short and unstructured, so node/edge decisions are straightforward, but some causal links are necessarily interpreted from wording rather than explicit statements.

Inference strategy justification:
Moderate inference (edge confidence = 2) was used only where causal ordering had to be made explicit (e.g., “low hope in policy solutions” enabling “diversified research directions”). All interventions and concepts appear directly or implicitly in the text.

Extraction completeness explanation:
Every distinct claim that supports a chain from the top-level risk (catastrophic ruin) through intermediate reasoning (optimization pressure, security mindset, difficulty, policy pessimism, diversification) to each actionable intervention (fund independent research, develop formal frameworks, train researchers in security mindset) is captured; all nodes are interconnected, and each has at least one edge.

Key limitations:
• Source gives no quantitative evidence, so edge confidences remain low-to-medium.  
• Interventions are described at a high level; implementation specifics are inferred only to the extent warranted by the text.  
• A longer source might reveal additional sub-mechanisms or interventions not captured here.
